fact: On 22 January 2025 the National Communication Authority directed all internet service providers to block access to all social media accounts for 30 to 90 days after unrest over footage of killings in Sudan; Zain and MTN told users Facebook and TikTok were no longer accessible, and CPJ's sources said both were unreachable without a VPN on 23 January; the regulator's director general said on 23 January it might be lifted within 72 hours.
system: Facebook and TikTok (social media block ordered by the National Communication Authority)

fact: AMDISS, a South Sudanese media body, publicly criticised the Facebook and TikTok blockage as restraining press freedom and public discourse.
AMDISS says Facebook and TikTok were blocked in South Sudan and urges the National Communication Authority to expedite lifting the ban.

Digital Rights Frontlines, a Juba-based group, publicly criticised gaps in the Cybercrimes and Computer Misuse Bill 2024, saying its defamation, surveillance and content provisions risk silencing critics.
CPJ says that in 2025 authorities suspended social media to block news from neighbouring Sudan.
Access Now lists South Sudan among 15 African countries where internet shutdowns were implemented in 2025.
CIVICUS Monitor says the Media Authority suspended the online outlet Hot in Juba on 6 October 2025 for publishing allegedly reckless and defamatory content.
CIVICUS Monitor says the online outlet Hot in Juba publicly criticised the Media Authority's suspension of it as unfair and a violation of media freedom, on 20 November 2025.

The South Sudan Human Rights Defenders Network and CEPO publicly criticised the Cybercrime and Computer Misuse Bill 2025 on 23 October 2025, warning of vague false-information offences and demanding a public hearing.
